# bundle


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A freezer’s output does not always run as it is, and it is often larger
than it needs to be. This module fixes a bundle after the freezer has
written it. Most of the work is for macOS, where py2app leaves more to
fix.
[`finish`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#finish),
near the end of the page, runs the repairs in order and is the function
most callers need. The steps are also available one by one, so each can
be run and tested on its own.
[`sign`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#sign) comes
last, after
[`finish`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#finish).

### graft

``` python
def graft(
    app, name, python:NoneType=None
):
```

*Copy the installed package `name` into a built bundle, replacing the
freezer’s copy, and return where it went.*

py2app puts pure Python modules into a zip archive inside the bundle,
`pythonXY.zip`, and Python imports them from there. Some packages do not
work from a zip: they read their own files from disk, or they carry
native programs and libraries that must exist as real files. Copying
such a package into the bundle after the freezer has run is called
grafting.

[`graft`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#graft)
copies the installed package `name` from the environment kavacha runs in
into the bundle’s `lib/pythonX.Y` folder, deletes whatever the freezer
left in its place, and returns where it put the package, relative to the
bundle. It stops with an error if the package is not installed or if the
bundle was built for a different Python version than `python`, which
defaults to the running one.

It also compiles the copied files to bytecode in unchecked-hash mode.
Python loads such `.pyc` files without comparing them to the source. A
signed bundle is read-only, and without these files Python would try to
write bytecode into it the first time the package is imported.

``` python
app, lib = mkapp('Demo.app')
(lib/'json.cpython-311-x86_64-linux-gnu.so').write_text('what the freezer flattened')
graft(app, 'json')
```

    Path('Contents/Resources/lib/python3.11/json')

[`graft`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#graft) finds
the `lib/pythonX.Y` folder in either layout: under
`Contents/Resources/lib` in a macOS app, or under `lib` in a Windows
build.

``` python
(root/'Win'/'lib'/ver).mkdir(parents=True)
_lib_dir(root/'Win').relative_to(root)
```

    Path('Win/lib/python3.11')

### link_duplicates

``` python
def link_duplicates(
    app, names, floor:int=1000000
):
```

*Hardlink identical files of at least `floor` bytes across the packages
in `names`, and return the megabytes saved.*

Some packages ship identical large files. playwright and patchright, for
example, each carry the same Node.js executable.
[`link_duplicates`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#link_duplicates)
looks through the packages in `names`, finds files of at least `floor`
bytes (1 MB by default) with the same content, and replaces each later
copy with a hardlink to the first, so the data is stored once. It
returns the megabytes saved.
[`finish`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#finish)
runs it over the grafted packages.

``` python
app2, lib2 = mkapp('Link.app')
node = os.urandom(2_000_000)                          
for n in ('playwright', 'patchright'):
    (lib2/n).mkdir(); (lib2/n/'node').write_bytes(node)
link_duplicates(app2, ['playwright', 'patchright'])
```

    2

### strip_zip

``` python
def strip_zip(
    app, prefixes:tuple=()
):
```

*Delete the entries that start with any of `prefixes` from the bundle’s
zip archive, and return the megabytes saved.*

Once a package is grafted, the freezer’s copy of it in the zip archive
is never imported, but it still takes up space. So does code nothing
reaches, such as the standard library’s tests.
[`strip_zip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#strip_zip)
deletes every archive entry whose path starts with one of `prefixes`,
keeps the rest unchanged, and returns the megabytes saved. A prefix is
matched as plain text, so end it with `/` to remove a single package.
The example removes `json/` and keeps `jsonschema`; the prefix `json`
would have removed both.

``` python
app4, lib4 = mkapp('Zip.app')
z = lib4.parent/zipname
with zipfile.ZipFile(z, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as f:
    f.writestr('json/decoder.py', os.urandom(3_000_000))
    f.writestr('jsonschema/_types.py', 'another package that starts with json')
    f.writestr('kavacha/window.py', 'the app itself')
strip_zip(app4, ('json/',))
```

    3

``` python
with zipfile.ZipFile(z) as f: kept = f.namelist()
kept
```

    ['jsonschema/_types.py', 'kavacha/window.py']

### install_modern_icon

``` python
def install_modern_icon(
    app, icon, identity:NoneType=None, deployment_target:str='14.0'
):
```

*Install an Icon Composer `.icon` into the bundle before signing,
keeping the `.icns` icon as the fallback.*

macOS 26 introduced a new kind of app icon, made with Apple’s Icon
Composer and saved as a `.icon` folder.
[`install_modern_icon`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#install_modern_icon)
adds such an icon to a built bundle with the iconmage tool and keeps the
`.icns` icon for older systems. It changes the bundle, so it must run
before signing. When `icon` is empty or not a folder it does nothing.
When iconmage is not installed, or the install fails, it prints why,
leaves the `.icns` icon in place and returns `None`. The example runs on
a machine without iconmage.

``` python
(root/'Demo.icon').mkdir()
install_modern_icon(app, root/'Demo.icon') is None
```

      iconmage not installed; keeping the ICNS icon alone (uv tool install git+https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/iconmage.git)

    True

### is_macho

``` python
def is_macho(
    p
):
```

*Whether `p` starts with a Mach-O or universal header.*

Compiled programs and libraries on macOS are Mach-O files. A Mach-O file
begins with load commands, a header that lists its segments, its code
signature, its install name (the path other programs use to find it),
its version, a UUID and the libraries it depends on. A universal file
holds one Mach-O slice per CPU architecture.

[`is_macho`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#is_macho)
checks whether a file starts with a Mach-O header.
[`macho`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#macho) reads
the header of each slice and returns those facts as a list of dicts, or
`None` for a file that is not Mach-O.
[`corrupt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#corrupt)
reports a file whose header does not describe its body, for example one
whose last segment does not end where the file does. `codesign` refuses
to sign such a file and reports “main executable failed strict
validation”. The example reads the system’s own `/usr/lib/dyld` when it
exists, which is the case on a Mac.

``` python
l = Path('/usr/lib/dyld')
is_macho(l) and [(s['type'], s['seg_end'] == s['size']) for s in macho(l)], corrupt(l)
```

### mend_frameworks

``` python
def mend_frameworks(
    app, search:tuple=()
):
```

*Replace each corrupt library in `Contents/Frameworks` with a healthy
installed copy, and report file names with more than one build
installed.*

py2app copies the native libraries a bundle needs into
`Contents/Frameworks` and names each copy by its file name alone. When
two different libraries share a file name, for example two builds of the
same library shipped by two packages, the copies get mixed up: one file
ends up with the body of one library and the header of the other, which
makes it corrupt in the sense above.

[`mend_frameworks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#mend_frameworks)
finds each corrupt file in `Contents/Frameworks` and replaces it with a
healthy installed copy. It looks among the libraries the interpreter and
the bundled packages link to, plus any folders in `search`, and prefers
a copy the same size as the corrupt file, then the highest version. It
then points the copy’s install name and dependencies at
`Contents/Frameworks` and signs it ad hoc.

It returns two dicts. `mended` maps each repaired file name to the copy
used, or to `None` when no healthy copy was found. `clashes` lists every
file name that has more than one distinct build installed on this
machine, whether or not it caused a problem this time. The example
bundle has no Frameworks folder, so both are empty.

``` python
app6, _ = mkapp('Mend.app')
mend_frameworks(app6)
```

### sign

``` python
def sign(
    app, identity, entitlements:NoneType=None, run:NoneType=None
):
```

*Code-sign every Mach-O file deepest first, then each framework, then
the bundle, signing hardlinked files once and never using `--deep`.*

macOS only runs a downloaded app if it is signed, and the signature has
to cover every program and library inside it.
[`sign`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#sign) signs
the bundle with `identity`, the name of your signing certificate, or `-`
for an ad hoc signature that only works on your own machine. It signs
each Mach-O file first, deepest in the folder tree first, then each
`.framework`, then the bundle, and finally verifies the result. It does
not use `codesign --deep`, which would sign everything with the same
options. Every file is signed with the hardened runtime
(`--options runtime`), which Apple’s notarisation requires.

Executables get the `entitlements` file, as the bundle does. Libraries
ending in `.so` or `.dylib` do not. Files that are hardlinks of one
another are signed once: `codesign --force` writes a new file, which
breaks the link, so
[`sign`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#sign) links
the other paths back to the signed file.

[`run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#run) is the
function that runs each command. The example passes one that records the
commands instead of running them, so it needs no certificate.

``` python
app7 = root/'Sign.app'
for rel in ('Contents/MacOS/Sign', 'Contents/Resources/lib/a/node', 'Contents/Resources/lib/x.so'):
    (p := app7/rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); p.write_bytes(b'\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe' + bytes(28))
(app7/'Contents/Resources/lib/a/node').chmod(0o755)
os.link(app7/'Contents/Resources/lib/a/node', app7/'Contents/Resources/lib/b')
calls = []
sign(app7, 'ID', 'ent.plist', run=lambda *a: calls.append([str(x) for x in a]))
[c[-1].replace(str(root), '') for c in calls]
```

### finish

``` python
def finish(
    app, spec, identity:NoneType=None
):
```

*Run every repair a frozen bundle needs, in order, and return what each
step did.*

[`finish`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#finish)
runs the repairs above in the order they depend on each other. It grafts
each package in `spec.grafted`, deletes their copies and the
`spec.unreachable` prefixes from the zip archive, hardlinks duplicate
files in the grafted packages, repairs `Contents/Frameworks`, and
installs `spec.modern_icon` if there is one. It returns a dict with the
result of each step, which
[`build`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#build)
prints. It does not sign the bundle, so call
[`sign`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#sign)
afterwards.

``` python
app5, lib5 = mkapp('Fin.app')
with zipfile.ZipFile(lib5.parent/zipname, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as f:
    f.writestr('json/decoder.py', os.urandom(2_000_000))
    f.writestr('test/test_json.py', os.urandom(1_000_000))
    f.writestr('kavacha/window.py', 'the app itself')
finish(app5, App('Demo', 'app.py', grafted=['json'], unreachable=['test/']))
```

    {'json': 'Contents/Resources/lib/python3.11/json',
     'stripped_mb': 3,
     'linked_mb': 0,
     'modern_icon': False}

The grafted `json` package is now a folder in `lib`, and the archive
keeps neither its old copy nor the `test/` entries marked as
unreachable.

``` python
with zipfile.ZipFile(lib5.parent/zipname) as f: left = f.namelist()
left, (lib5/'json'/'decoder.py').exists()
```

    (['kavacha/window.py'], True)

### frozen_distribution

``` python
def frozen_distribution():
```

*Return a setuptools `Distribution` class that ignores the dependencies
the project declares.*

py2app runs from a `setup.py`, through setuptools. setuptools also reads
the project’s `pyproject.toml`, so the dependencies listed there become
requirements of the freeze, alongside what the
[`App`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#app) says.
[`frozen_distribution`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/bundle.html#frozen_distribution)
returns a setuptools `Distribution` class that empties
`install_requires` after the configuration has been read, so the
[`App`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#app) is the only
description of what goes into the bundle. Pass it to `setup` as
`distclass`.

``` python
d = frozen_distribution()({'name': 'demo', 'install_requires': ['fastcore']})
d.parse_config_files()
d.install_requires
```

    []
